/* Fundamental screen, filter first (responsive redesign). Reads out/fundamentals.json only and never changes a value: the filters only choose which rows are shown.
   Strict numbers: a stored value passes an active numeric filter only if it is a finite JSON number. Missing, blank, "-", text and non-finite values never pass.
   A box left empty means "any". Anything typed must be a plain number of 0 or more (12, 12.5, .5), or the screen says so and shows no rows until it is fixed.
   P/E: a P/E range (or "Positive only") lists positive P/E only, so a loss-making company's negative P/E is never read as a cheap valuation; "Negative only"
   lists the loss-making ones on request. P/E of exactly 0 is neither. Sorting by P/E puts zero and negative P/E after the positive ones.
   P/B follows the same rule: a P/B range (or "Positive only") lists positive P/B only, "Negative only" lists negative book value on request, and sorting puts zero
   and negative P/B after the positive ones. Load more: each screen table shows 50 matching rows, then "Show 50 more". Sector: an exact match on the published sector; a stock without one never passes a chosen sector.
   The other tabs (Financial Health, Cash Flow & Growth) use the same rules through window.SLScreen. */

if(!j||!Array.isArray(j.stocks)||!j.stocks.length)throw new Error("empty");FD=j.stocks.filter(x=>x&&typeof x==="object");                 /* every published row is kept; only an empty (null) entry, which has nothing to show, is skipped */
FD.forEach(x=>{if(typeof x.symbol==="string")FBY[x.symbol]=x});
